full_judgment:
Mir Hashmat Ali, J: In the instant Rule, the petitioner challenged the judgment and order dated 17.2.2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 rejecting the prayer under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for stay of the subsequent Judge (Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Dhaka.

2. The petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, title and interest of 2/3 share in the eastern portion of the 3 schedule property and for cancellation of the Tamizuddin Khan Trust Deed No. 5915 dated 6.3.1985 and for permanent injunction restraining the Defendant No. 1 from claiming the title over the schedule property.

3. The schedule as has been stated in the said Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 runs thus" one storied" pucca building measuring approximately 8,400 sqf. on plot no. 22/1. Block-B.Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Mouja Barba, P.S. Mohammadpur, Measuring about 1000 sqf. yards now known as No. 1, Babar Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. In the said suit Mrs. U.K. Siddiqua Huda was shown as principal Defendant and Mrs. Razia Khan Amin and Mrs. Nina Jamaly as proforma Defendants.

4. After appearance in the said suit the Tamizuddin Khan Trust represented by its chairman filed title Suit No. 237 of 2002 against the Devendant Zaber Siddique, Adnan Siddique, Moulana Mohammad Baker Siddique Jounpuri, Babor Sidique before the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration that the 'A' Schedule property as stressed property, a decree for khas possession of the B & C schedule property after evicting the Defendants, a decree for permanent injunction 'restraining the Defendants from evicting the tenant of the plaintiff from the 'D' schedule property and changing the natured and character of the vacant land and giving lease or transfer or construct any stracture in the 'C' schedule property to any other party and for a declaration for profit of Taka 20,000/- per month.

5. Defendant No. 3 after appearance of Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 filed an application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 14.11. 2002 stating that regarding the same schedule property Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 is pending before the same Court to determine the same issues between the same parties and as such the subsequent suit being Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 should be stayed till disposal of Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 now pending before the same court.

6. The plaintiff filed written objection against the said application dated 14.11.2002 denying the assertion made by the Defendant No. 3 of Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 stating that the Tamizuddin Khan Trust deed was created with the consent of the Defendant No. 3 who was a signatory in the deed. It was further stated that the parties of both the suit are not same. In the earlier suit Tamizuddin Khan Trust Estate was not made party in the suit and Mrs. U.K. Siddiqua Huda, Mrs. Razia Khan Amin and Mrs. Nina Jamely are not party in the subsequent suit. Zabbar Siddique, Adnan Siddiqui and Babor Siddique are not the party in the earlier Title Suit No. 371d of 1998. The schedules are not the same, which are apparent in the plaint of both the suits. The reliefs claimed are not the same, which are apparent from the paper of both the suits. The relief claimed in the subsequent suit cannot be granted in the previous instituted suit. The title as claimed in both the suits is different. The issues, which will be settled in both the suits, are also different. It was further stated that if the earlier suit fails, the Plaintiff of the subsequent suit will not get any relief and that the application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is premature.

7. The trial Court after hearing the parties and on consideration of the materials on record rejected the said application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure by his judgment and order dated 17.2.2003 in Title Suit No. 237 of 2002.

8. Against the said order dated 17.2.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title suit No. 237 of 2002 the Defendant No. 3 preferred application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained instant Rule.

9. Mr. Md. Musherrof Hossain Majumdar, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that Defendant No. 3 Moulana Mohammad Baquer Siddiqui Jonpuri filed Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 before the learned Subordinate Judge (joint District Judge), 2nd Court Dhaka for declaration of right, title and interest over the suit property and permanent injunction and for cancellation of the truest deed No. 5915 dated 6.3.1985. In the said suit who are beneficiary of the Trust deed were made party as Defendant Nos. 1-3. He further submits that point of both the suits to be decided as to whether the trust deed is a genuine document or not and as such the issues in both the suits are same and the parties of both the suits are same and the schedule property in both the suits are same and as such the subsequent suit being, Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 to be stayed to avoid the multiplicity of the proceeding.

10. Mr. Khalilur Rahman, Learned Advocate appearing with Mr. T.M. Sakil Hossain submits that the trial Court on consideration all the aspect of the case has rightly rejected the application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The trial Court considered that the parties involve in both the suits are different. The issues are also different. He further submits that the plaint of Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 shows that the schedules are also different. The relief claimed in both the suits are different. He further submits that the relief claimed in the subsequent suit cannot be granted in the previously instituted suit. The title of the suit are also different; cause of action arrived in both the suits are different. The title of the suit are also different; cause of action arrived in both the suits are different. The issues are to be framed in two suits are different. He further submits that if the earlier suit being Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 is failed. The plaintiff of the subsequent suit in Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 will not get any, relief and the relief claimed in the subsequent suit will be barred by limitation. He further submits that Defendant No. 3d without submitting the written statement in the subsequent suit has filed the application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such at this stage it cannot be said that the issues of the subsequent suit are same. He further submits that the issue will be framed according to the relief claimed by the parties and on consideration of written statement. Lastly, he Submits that the application under section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a pre-matured one. Until and unless the issues are framed by the Courts below in both the suits it cannot be said that the issues are same. In support of his contention he cited the case of Askar Ali and another Vs. Shamsul Islam alias Md. Shamsuddin and others reported in 4 MLR(AD)-193.

11. We have heard the learned Advocates at length and perused the revisional application and the grounds there under and papers and documents and annexures of the application and the counter affidavit filed by opposite party No. 1.

12. It appears that Begum Atika Khanam, the wife of late Tamizuddin Khan created Tamizuddin Khan Trust Estate vide trust deed No. 5915 dated 3.6.1985. The defendant No. 3 challenged the said trust deed in Title Suit No: 371 of 1998 by making defendant No. 1 Mrs. U.K. Siddiqui Huda. Mrs. Razia Khan Amin, Mrs. Nina Jamaly. Thus Defendants appeared in the suit and filed written statement denying the allegations made in the plaint. While the said suit was pending for disposal Tamizuddin Khan Trust itself filed Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 praying for declaration that the 'A' schedule property is a trusted property after evicting the Defendants, a decree for permanent injunction restraining the Defendants from evicting the tenants from the schedule property by the defendants forcefully and from changing the nature and character of the suit property in order to giving lease to any other persons or for transferring newly constructed 10 shops to the 3rd party as described in the schedule 'G' and a decree for monthly profit of Taka 20,000/- per months against the Defendants.

13. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 being Defendant No. 3 of Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 filed an application under Section 10 of the Civil Procedure (Annexure—'C') praying for stay Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 till ,disposal of Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 stating that the schedule property is the same and parties of both the suits are same and issues are the same but we find that the earlier suit was field against the Defendant No. 1 Mrs. U.K. Siddique Huda Defendant No. 2 Mrs. Razia Khan Amin, Defendant No. 3 Mrs. Nina Jamaly who are not made party in the subsequently instituted suit. It further appears that Kabir Siddique, Adnan Siddiqui and Babor Siddiqui are also not made party in the earlier instituted suit and as such it cannot be said that both the suits are related between the same parties.

14. It appears from the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 which are as follows:

Schedule of the property.

One three storied, pucca building measuring approximately 8400 sft. on plot No. 22/1, Block-B, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Mouza Baraba, P.S. Tejgaon, District-Dhaka measuring about 1000 sq. yeards now address as No. 1, Babar Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka.

The schedule of subsequent Title suit No. 237 of 2002 are as follows:

SCHEDULE—' A'

All that piece and parcel of 4800 sft, or 0.20625 acre (1000 sq. yrds) non agricultural land appear training to Housing and settlement plot No. 22/1 of Block-B, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Mouza- Tejgaon at present Mohammadpur, District-Dhaka commonly known as No. Babar Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka with three storied building and all its appurtenances which has been shown by red border line in the attached sketch map.

SCHEDULE—`B’

Out of the said 'A' schedule entire property two bed rooms , one drawing room, one kitchem room, one dining room, one store room, two bath rooms and one dreassing room of the ground floor which has been shown by bellow border line in the attached sketch map.

SCHEDULE—`C’

Out of the 'A' schedule entire property 7 (seven) semi pucca under construction shop rooms facing to the Mirpur road and another 3(three) under construction shop room facing to the Babor road as shown by colour sky blue in attached sketch map.

SCHEDULE-‘D’

The 1st and 2nd floor and the 3(three) garages of the ground floor and 3 store rooms upon the said garages and vacant place out the 'A' schedule property which is under the possession of monthly tenant, Directorate of Archaeology.

15. The schedule as has been described in Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 has been described by hand made sketch as such we find that the schedule of both the suits are not same. It further appears that the cause of action of both the suits are different. The relief claimed in the earlier Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 the plaintiff prayed for declaration of right, title and interest over the suit property to the extended of share and for cancellation of Tamizuddin Khan Trust deed No. 5915 dated 6.3.1985 and for permanent injunction against the Defendant claiming the right, title and interest over the schedule property. It appears from the prayer of the Title Suit No. 371 of 1998 that the Defendants No. 3 claimed 2/3 share of the schedule property and as such we find that share of the schedule property admittedly remains with the Defendants Nos. 1-3.

16. The prayer as stated in the plaint of the subsequently instituted Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 that the Trust claims a decree over the 'A' schedule property. Recovery of khas possession 'B' and 'C' schedule property permanent injunction against 'D' and 'E' schedule property and as such we find that the reliefs claimed are not the same.

<u>17. We find that the issues has not yet been framed in both the suits even Defendant No. 3 of Title Suit No. 237 of 2002 has not yet submitted any written statement and as such it cannot be said at this stage that the issues are same. It has been held in the case of Askar Ali and another Vs. Shamsul Islam alias Md. Shamsuddin and others reported in 4 MLR(AD)-193 that the subsequent suit may be stayed only when the matter in issue of the previously instituted suit is directly and substantially the same, the parties are the same title and the court is competent to grant the relief so claimed. Unless the Court is satisfied with the above tests of law, no stay can be granted. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No.1 submits that if the earlier suit fails or in the alternative the plaintiff of the earlier suits unable to get a decree the plaintiff of the subsequent suit will not set relief due to the law of limitation. Such submission merits consideration. We find that both the suits are not between the same parties; not in the same schedule; not with the same cause of action not with the same prayer; though no issues are framed, the issues may not be same. The relief claimed in subsequent suit cannot be determined and granted in previously instantiated suit. From the facts and circumstances of the case as discussed above we do not find any reason to interfere in the impugned judgment and order passed by the trial Court.</u>

18. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The order of stay granted by this Court stands vacated. The trial Court is directed to expedite the trial of both the suits.

19. Communicate the order at once.

End.
